title: Locally constant finite type sheaves form a weak Serre subcategory
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The full subcategory of sheaves of $\underline B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which are locally constant of finite type is closed under kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and under extensions in the abelian category of sheaves of $\underline B$-modules. Here $\underline B$ is the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]; locally constant of finite type means that locally on the site the sheaf is isomorphic to the constant sheaf associated to a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. No existence of points of the site is assumed.

proof.text: For every sheaf define its sieve of finite constant trivializations. It is a sieve because a local isomorphism restricts through the canonical successive-restriction isomorphism. The finite-type local-constancy predicate is equivalent to this sieve being covering on every object. Intersect two trivializing covers and use transitivity to work with constant source and target on one slice. Restriction to that slice is exact.

For the kernel and cokernel, conjugate the sheaf morphism through these local trivializations. Local linearity supplies a further cover on which it is induced by g:M→N. Exactness of restriction and of the constant functor identifies the restricted kernel and cokernel with constants of ker g and coker g. The kernel is finite by Noetherianity; the cokernel is finite as a quotient. Cover transitivity proves the two closure assertions.

For an extension, intersect trivializing covers for its outer terms. On such a slice apply the local constant-presentation theorem, whose proof carries out the finite-free choice, local lifting, and cokernel presentation of source steps 3–5. It produces on a covering sieve finite K,Q and an isomorphism from the middle sheaf to coker(a) for a:constant(K)|V→constant(Q)|V.
Apply local linearity once more to the finite-source presentation map a. On a further covering sieve its conjugated restriction is constant(g) for a B-linear g:K→Q.

Restrict the chosen cokernel isomorphism using exactness of further restriction between slices. The cokernel-map comparison under the successive-restriction isomorphisms identifies this restricted cokernel with coker(constant(g)|W). Exactness of the constant functor and of slice restriction then identifies it with constant(coker(g))|W.

The coefficient cokernel is finite as a quotient of Q. It therefore supplies a member of the middle sheaf's trivialization sieve. Cover transitivity through all refinements proves extension closure. Empty covers are handled by sieve transitivity and finite rank zero by the finite-biproduct argument, with no points or splittings assumed.
